subject: Request: Upfront bill-credit for NexaScale onramp — exec clearance
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Nguyen <elaine.nguyen@nexascale.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed onboarding credit structure for pilot

Hi Elaine —

Thanks again for the meeting last week. As discussed, we put together a short onramp proposal to get NexaScale into a production pilot quickly while keeping near-term unit economics reasonable for both teams. The key ask from your side was an upfront billing credit to soften first-quarter spend while you validate throughput and latency with your models.

High level proposal: 
- Pilot term: 3 months, up to 4M tokens/month
- Upfront billing credit: USD 40k applied to Q1 invoices, repayable as a usage offset over months 2–6 if thresholds are met
- Commitment: 6-month minimum support window + preferred capacity burst

Attached: Onramp schedule and draft SOW. If this looks aligned, I can start the internal approval thread to request an exception to our standard non-refundable billing policy — this will require VP/CFO sign-off due to the size and repayment mechanics.

Next steps: please confirm acceptance of the structure or flag any items you want adjusted. I can route legal for a short SOW after that.

Cheers,
Jordan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
(j) 415-555-0194

Attachments: NexaScale_Onramp_Schedule_v2.xlsx; SOW_NexaScale_v1.pdf

From: Elaine Nguyen <elaine.nguyen@nexascale.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 08:42:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Proposed onboarding credit structure for pilot

Jordan —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. The structure looks promising and addresses the internal procurement concerns about first-quarter spend. Two small asks from our side before we proceed to signature:

1) Can the upfront credit be split 50/50 between an invoice credit and a committed integration services credit? Our finance team prefers to see part of it allocated to services so it shows up as a different line item. 
2) Can we get a hard SLA for startup throughput (5k TPS per GPU) during the pilot window — we'll need that in the SOW.

If you can confirm those, I will pull procurement and Tom Hirsch (our external contract counsel) into the loop and we can aim to sign the SOW by the end of next week.

Best,
Elaine
Head of Platform Partnerships
NexaScale

Marissa / Laura —

Quick heads up: NexaScale (prospect) has asked for the upfront credit to be split between invoice credit and services credit and wants a hard throughput SLA in the SOW. The total economic impact is ~USD 40k upfront, with repayment mechanics that would reduce recognized revenue in Q1 and spread offsets over months 2–6. They are ready to sign quickly if we can accept the split and add the SLA.

Why approve:
- Strong strategic fit: high likelihood of expansion to a paid production contract in Q4 given their product roadmap.
- Short timeframe: they want to sign by next week; losing momentum risks them shopping alternatives.

Risks / controls: 
- We propose the services-credit be contractually tied to deliverables (integration milestones) and non-refundable if milestones are met; invoice credit only applies if usage thresholds are reached.
- Legal will include clawback language if they don't hit agreed usage.

Can we get a quick exec clearance? If we get VP/CFO signoff we can ship a revised SOW to Elaine and Tom. Rafael — can you run an econ calc and confirm the revenue recognition path?

Thanks,
Jordan

Attachments referenced: NexaScale_Billing_Credit_Term_Summary.docx

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: NexaScale asks — request for exception & VP/CFO signoff

Jordan / Marissa —

Short answer: I can support the exception with controls. Quick summary of the econ impact and accounting treatment: 

- USD 40k upfront split: 20k invoice credit; 20k services credit.
- Services credit treated as deferred revenue tied to milestone deliverables (integration complete, performance validation). When milestones are met we recognize the service revenue.
- Invoice credit applied against Q1 usage; if customer fails to hit 70% of the monthly threshold across the pilot, invoice credit is clawed back pro-rata.
- No material impact to ARR; cash collection timing shifts but we have controls.

Recommend path: Exec signoff (VP/CFO) to allow the exception with the following gating items: 
1) Legal-approved clawback and milestone definitions in SOW
2) Finance to own deferred revenue schedule and monthly usage audits
3) Sales to capture a short mutual action plan in HubSpot linking milestones + acceptance criteria.

If you want, I can draft the finance note for Marissa to include in the approval request to VP/CFO.

-Rafael
Finance Manager | Redwood Inference
